card.name: Merengue
card.era: Mid-19th century to present; national symbol under Trujillo
card.tagline: The national music and partner dance of the Dominican Republic.
card.profile: Merengue is the national music and dance of the Dominican Republic, danced in pairs in a 2/4 rhythm with a steady marching/side-to-side basic step and characteristic hip motion from weight changes. The core conjunto tipico features the diatonic accordion, the tambora (two-headed drum) and the guira (metal scraper) - symbolizing European, African and Taino cultures. Flirtatious gestures accompany the dance; it pervades daily life from celebrations to political campaigning. On 26 November 2005 the DR president decreed a National Merengue Day (UNESCO; English Wikipedia).
card.insight: UNESCO inscribed 'Music and dance of the merengue in the Dominican Republic' in 2016 (file 01162), noting it attracts people of different social classes and promotes coexistence among communities (UNESCO).

steps.name: Basic Merengue Steps
steps.description: Stepping and dragging feet while bending alternating knees

steps.name: Basic Turn
steps.description: Clockwise turn with loose hand grip and elbow down

cues: bend one knee at the time
keep your feet flat on the floor
common_mistakes: hitting each other's legs when bending knees
letting hand go during turns (spaghetti arms)
safety: keep elbows down to prevent accidents from happening
lessons.teacher_style: Ricardo and Elba teach with clear step-by-step breakdowns, combining historical context with detailed biomechanical instructions. They use visual aids, partner demonstrations, and positive reinforcement to guide students through basic Merengue steps and turns.
lessons.distinctive_method: Using illustrated graphic overlays that appear on screen to emphasize key body positions, knee bends, and footwork while the instructor speaks.
what_hinders: some transitions between solo and partner work are fast

evidence.observation: Instructor demonstrates posture with hands on waist and slight knee bending
